reuse.why: Extends the existing getExpectedScheduleAmount/getScheduledAmount pair and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance.

duplication.why: No new copy of the rule, but updateActions keeps its own `typeof number ? value : helper` dispatch, so its approximate case never reaches the helper, and forecast adds its own op fallback.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the range rule, but it is opt-in through an optional op parameter that each caller must remember to pass.

scope.why: Only the helper, its callers that already pass amounts, a type field and tests.

maintainability.why: An optional, untyped `op?: string` appended after `inverse` makes it easy to forget, and the desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount silently keep the old behaviour.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts updateActions returns numeric amounts itself before calling getExpectedScheduleAmount, so the op it now passes is never used for approximate amounts

disguised_duplication.where: the leftover per-site dispatch is pre-existing and unchanged, not reshaped

one_place.where: defined once in getExpectedScheduleAmount, but applied only when callers pass op: updateActions short-circuits numbers, and desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, MobileSchedulesPage.tsx, SchedulesListItem.tsx) pass no op
